_about: Agent roles: which agent does each job, and how it must be dispatched. Shipped defaults.
A role names a job, not an agent. 'providers' is an ordered preference list; the first one installed is used.
Dispatch by role with subagent_type 'role:<role>', or 'role:<job>:<role>' from a team job (for example role:refactor:engineer); or by the agent's own name, and the rules below still apply.

Resolution order (docs/PROJECT-TEAM.md, "Roles"): the repo binding's 'roles', then the personal agent-roles.json in the machine folder, then this file. At each level the key '<job>:<role>' is tried before '<role>'. A level naming only agents that are not installed is skipped and logged.

When no level matches, a review role (reviewer, code-review) goes to the built-in general-purpose agent, never to the session that did the work. Any other role is denied, and the session does the work itself.
Put an owner- or employer-specific provider in the personal agent-roles.json in the machine folder, never here: this file is published.
Enforced by runtime/agent-roles.py (PreToolUse on Agent, SubagentStop), using runtime/team_roles.py. Edit the tables, not the hook.
model: forced on every dispatch of the role. Put [model-approved] in the dispatch description to keep a different model for one dispatch.
nested_model: ceiling for agents the role's agent spawns itself (opus, or no model given, is lowered to this).

prompt_append: added to the dispatch prompt once; {reviews} in it becomes the binding's 'reviews' folder (default axis/runs/). run_record: the agent may not stop until it has written a record folder under the binding's 'reviews' (default axis/runs/). When the role is also a job in runtime/record-contracts.json (the reviewer), each folder at any depth under 'reviews' in which it wrote a file the job marks (findings*.md) must hold the job's artefacts: for a reviewer, its mutation record beside each findings file (findings.md owes mutations.json, findings-fix1.md owes mutations-fix1.json), in the mutation-record format, written during the run for each findings file the run wrote. A findings file has one of the names record-contracts.json declares (rounds); a findings-like file under another name is refused.

prediction_record: the '<job>:<role>' dispatches that may not stop until the record folder their brief names ('Record folder:', else the binding's folder for the 'Work order <id>:') holds a moves.prediction<R>.json that predict-gate's checker accepts and that names a move. A dispatch by the resolved agent's plain name is held to it too when its brief has a 'Work order <id>:' line. Read from this file only, so no binding or personal table can remove it. predict-gate.sh close is the hard gate.

spend_kinds: the kinds a spend row may carry that are not roles. spend.sh record --kind takes one of this table's roles or one of these, and nothing else: the one closed list (docs/PROJECT-TEAM.md, "Gate refusals"). 'answering-agent' answers open rows. 'agent' names no role: it is kept for old rows, backfilled rows and corrections that keep it, and a new first record may not take it ("newRecords": false). 'no-role' is an agent that ran in no role (Explore, an ad-hoc general-purpose agent, a fork), so every agent can be recorded.
